title: Background Task Queue
description: Build a background job queue with priority levels, scheduled jobs, retry with backoff, and worker pools.

steps.title: Create Job Data Structure
steps.description: Define a `Job` class or factory function with fields: `id` (uuid or counter), `type` (string), `payload` (object), `priority` (1-10, lower = higher priority), `status` (pending/running/completed/failed), `createdAt`, and `attempts`. Create 3 sample jobs with different priorities and print their structure as formatted JSON.
hints: Use a simple counter for sequential IDs
Set initial status to 'pending' and attempts to 0
Use `JSON.stringify(job, null, 2)` for readable output

verification.successMessage: Job data structure has all required fields
verification.failureMessage: Job structure is missing required fields

steps.title: Implement Queue with Priority
steps.description: Build a `PriorityQueue` class that stores jobs in a min-heap ordered by priority (lowest number = highest priority). Implement `enqueue(job)` and `dequeue()` methods. Enqueue 5 jobs with mixed priorities and print the dequeue order to verify correct priority sorting.
hints: Use an array-based binary heap implementation
The parent of index i is at Math.floor((i - 1) / 2)
Bubble up on enqueue and sink down on dequeue to maintain heap property

verification.successMessage: Priority queue dequeues jobs in correct priority order
verification.failureMessage: Jobs were not dequeued in priority order

steps.title: Add Worker Pool
steps.description: Create a `WorkerPool` class that manages a fixed number of workers (e.g., 3). Workers pull jobs from the queue and process them concurrently. Each worker calls a `process(job)` function. Print `'Worker 1 processing: jobType'` when a worker starts a job and `'Worker 1 completed: jobType'` when finished.
hints: Use async/await — each worker runs an infinite loop dequeueing jobs
Limit concurrency by creating exactly N worker promises
Simulate async work with `await delay(ms)`

verification.successMessage: Worker pool correctly processes jobs concurrently
verification.failureMessage: Workers did not process jobs or output status

steps.title: Implement Retry with Exponential Backoff
steps.description: Add retry logic to the worker. If a job fails (the process function throws), increment the retry count and re-enqueue the job with a delay. Use exponential backoff: delays of 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s (max 3 retries). Print `'Retry attempt N for job X (delay: Ns)'` on each retry. Mark as 'failed' after max retries.
hints: Calculate delay as `Math.pow(2, attempt - 1) * 1000` ms
Wrap the process call in try/catch to detect failures
Use `setTimeout` or a delayed enqueue mechanism for scheduling retries

verification.successMessage: Retry with exponential backoff correctly retries failed jobs
verification.failureMessage: Retry logic did not execute as expected

steps.title: Add Scheduled/Delayed Jobs
steps.description: Implement a `schedule(job, timestamp)` method that holds jobs until their scheduled time. Store delayed jobs in a separate sorted list. A scheduler tick runs every second, moving due jobs from the delayed list into the main queue. Print `'Scheduled: job X at time'` and `'Moved to queue: job X'` when due.
hints: Keep delayed jobs in a sorted array by scheduled time
Use `setInterval` or `setTimeout` for the scheduler tick
Compare `Date.now()` against scheduled time to determine if a job is due

verification.successMessage: Scheduled jobs are held until their time then moved to the queue
verification.failureMessage: Delayed jobs were not scheduled or moved correctly

steps.title: Implement Job Events/Hooks
steps.description: Add an event system to the queue: `onComplete(jobId, callback)` and `onFailed(jobId, callback)`. When a job completes or fails after all retries, invoke the corresponding callback. Print `'Event: job X completed'` or `'Event: job X failed'` when events fire. Support wildcard listeners with `'*'` for all jobs.
hints: Store callbacks in a Map keyed by jobId or '*'
Trigger events after the job status changes
Pass the job object to the callback so handlers can inspect results

verification.successMessage: Job events fire correctly on completion and failure
verification.failureMessage: Job event hooks did not fire

steps.title: Build Queue Statistics
steps.description: Add statistics tracking to the queue: `processed` (total completed), `failed` (total failed), `retried` (total retries), `pending` (current queue size). Expose a `stats()` method. After running a mix of successful and failing jobs, print the stats report as formatted JSON.
hints: Increment counters in the worker after each job outcome
Update pending count from the queue's length property
Print `stats()` output as `JSON.stringify` for clean formatting

verification.successMessage: Queue statistics track all job lifecycle events
verification.failureMessage: Statistics output is missing expected fields
